name: Orecchiette with Italian Sausage and Broccoli
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Verified 599 cal / 26g protein at the source, clears both bars as written with no adjustment. Eight ingredients, all board-tracked, and broccoli is one of the cheapest vegetables on the board. Classic Puglian pairing the catalog does not have. Toss-and-divide pasta, scales cleanly. | HARVEST:
intro_html: Sausage and broccoli with cupped pasta is the classic pairing from Puglia, down in the heel of Italy, and it survives on six ingredients because it does not need any more than that. The pasta catches the broccoli and the sausage fat, garlic and parmesan do the rest. It comes in cheap at about $2.07 a bowl (at everyday cost), and it still carries 30 grams of protein.
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Pantry seasonings (black pepper, red pepper flakes, salt): ~$0.46. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $16.70 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.19 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $22.84 across 14 servings, roughly $1.63 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $6.08 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $28.92. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About $2.07 a bowl (at everyday cost). Six ingredients, one pot for the pasta, one pan for the sausage, and dinner is handled for two weeks.
shop_smart: Pasta shells stand in for orecchiette perfectly. Both are cupped shapes designed to trap sauce and small vegetables. Shells are usually a third the price of imported orecchiette.
Frozen broccoli florets are the smart buy here. No trimming, no waste, and they go straight into the pasta water for the last minutes of cooking.
Buy parmesan in a tub, not a wedge, for a batch this size. You are melting it into the pasta, not shaving it over a plate, so the finish does not matter.
Garlic, butter and red pepper flakes are the entire sauce. There is no cream, no jarred sauce, and no tomato in this dish, which is exactly why it costs so little.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Bring a large pot of well salted water to a boil. Salting the water is your only chance to season the pasta itself.
Boil the pasta shells, and add the broccoli florets to the same pot for the last few minutes so they cook in the pasta water.
Reserve a couple of mugs of that starchy water before draining, then drain the pasta and broccoli together.
While the pasta cooks, brown the hot Italian sausage in crumbles in a wide skillet until it takes on real color.
Add the butter and the minced garlic to the sausage along with the red pepper flakes and black pepper, and cook just until fragrant.
Return the drained pasta and broccoli to your big pot, pour the sausage and garlic butter over it, and add the parmesan.
Splash in the reserved pasta water a little at a time and toss hard. The starch and the cheese emulsify into a light sauce that coats everything.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty pot weight from Step 1. Divide that total by 14 and scoop the exact amount into each container, tossing the pot between scoops so the sausage spreads evenly. Every bowl lands near 564 calories and 30 grams of protein.

head.description: Puglian style pasta with hot Italian sausage, broccoli, garlic butter and parmesan. Six ingredients, 14 servings, 564 calories, 30g protein, about $2.07 each (at everyday cost).
head.keywords: orecchiette with sausage and broccoli, italian sausage pasta, broccoli pasta, cheap pasta dinner, budget meal prep
steps: Boil the pasta shells in well salted water, adding the broccoli florets for the last few minutes.
Reserve some starchy pasta water, then drain the pasta and broccoli together.
Brown the hot Italian sausage in crumbles in a wide skillet.
Add butter, minced garlic and red pepper flakes to the sausage and cook until fragrant.
Toss the pasta, broccoli, sausage and parmesan with splashes of the reserved pasta water until sauced.
